name: Kiln & Clay Pottery Studio
tagline: Pottery classes for beginners in Asheville, North Carolina
home: Kiln & Clay is a small pottery studio in Asheville. We teach wheel throwing and hand-building to beginners in classes of six or fewer.
Try a two-hour taster session, or join a six-week course. We fire and glaze your pieces and they're ready about three weeks later.
about: The studio is in a converted warehouse in the River Arts District.
We use a local stoneware clay and mix our own glazes.

posts.title: What to wear to your first pottery class
posts.description: Clothes, nails and jewelry: what to know before you come.
posts.body:
Clay gets everywhere, so plan for it.

## Clothes

Wear clothes you don't mind getting dirty. We lend aprons.

## Nails and jewelry

Long nails leave marks in the clay. Take off rings and watches.

## How long it takes

Your pieces need to dry and be fired twice, so they're ready about three weeks later.

posts.title: Wheel throwing vs hand-building
posts.description: Which one to start with, and what each is good for.
posts.body:
There are two main ways to shape clay.

## Hand-building

Pinching, coiling and slabs. You can make any shape, and it's forgiving for beginners.

## Wheel throwing

Shaping clay on a spinning wheel. Great for symmetrical pots, but centering the clay takes practice.

## Where to start

For a taster session, start with hand-building. Our six-week course covers both.
